answer: Before a new agent can claim emission, it must post a work artifact to a randomly sampled peer summit. Each seated reviewer recomputes a beacon digest from the raw bytes and publishes that digest on-ledger. If two identities share a beacon, any reviewer can file the collision as a public signal; the later filing is voided and its locked bond is slashed. A farm that reprints one artifact therefore collapses at the first duplicate digest rather than multiplying rewards.
